methodology: Every case runs an unmodified byte-for-byte copy of the real control_plane.py and validate_contracts.py as a real subprocess CLI, inside an isolated scratch repo tree per test (tempfile.TemporaryDirectory), never touching the shared ledger. See workstreams/po03/review/sonnet/attacks/scratch_control_plane.py and workstreams/po03/tests/test_a10_control_plane_attacks.py.
command_output: workstreams/po03/review/sonnet/coordinator-audit/run-log.txt (17 tests, all pass -- each test's own assertions encode whether HELD or BREAK/BOUNDARY was expected)

invariants.statement: A producer must not reach COMPLETED without coordinator ingestion.
invariants.evidence: cmd_complete requires unit['obzio_state'] == 'PARENT_INGESTED' (control_plane.py:620); calling `complete` on a leased-but-never-ingested unit raises ControlPlaneError.

invariants.statement: A stale fence token must not commit after ownership transfer.

sub_cases.evidence: A fence token strictly lower than the last recorded value is rejected with FENCE_REJECTED (control_plane.py:524-534).

ingest_result's only fence check is `if incoming_fence < unit['fence_token']` (control_plane.py:524). It never checks that `incoming_fence` was ever actually granted by a `lease` call. A unit that has never been leased has unit['fence_token'] == 0 by the project_units default (control_plane.py:272), so any self-chosen fence_token >= 1 passes -- a party that never held the lease can commit as if it did.
sub_cases.root_cause: Fencing is implemented as a monotonic-counter check, not as lease-holder-identity verification. There is no record consulted of *which* fence values were actually issued via `lease`, only the high-water mark.

invariants.statement: A duplicate callback must not produce two effects.

sub_cases.evidence: A byte-identical resubmission is recognised via sha256(canonical(result_doc)) matching a prior PARENT_INGESTED payload and recorded as DUPLICATE_IGNORED (control_plane.py:569-586); exactly one PARENT_INGESTED row exists.

Deduplication is keyed on the hash of the *entire* result document, not on task_id/idempotency_key. A unit already COMPLETED that receives a result document differing only in artifact bytes/result_commit_id/checkpoint_seq is not recognised as a duplicate, is re-ingested, and project_units' generic fallback `unit['obzio_state'] = row.get('obzio_state') or event` (control_plane.py:326-327) resets the projected state from COMPLETED back to PARENT_INGESTED with no monotonicity guard against regressing from a terminal state. `complete` can then be called a second time, producing two COMPLETED ledger rows for one unit_id with two different result_commit_id values.
sub_cases.root_cause: (a) dedup keys on full-document hash instead of a stable content-independent identity; (b) the state projection has no 'COMPLETED is terminal, cannot be re-entered' rule.

invariants.statement: An artifact must not pass read-back without matching bytes.
invariants.evidence: sha256_file(target) is recomputed and compared to the claimed hash (control_plane.py:561-566); a missing file raises before hashing (control_plane.py:559-560). Both a corrupted-content and a deleted-artifact fixture are rejected.
invariants.boundary: Stopped at control_plane.py lines 559-566, PROVIDED `target` resolves to the intended path -- see INV-6, where this guarantee is shown to fail.

invariants.statement: A result must not be accepted if it references a dispatch manifest it was not issued under.
invariants.evidence: ingest_result compares result_doc['immutable_input_manifest_sha256'] to the dispatch record's own value looked up by task_id (control_plane.py:540-543) and rejects a mismatch, including a hash copied verbatim from a different real unit's dispatch record.

invariants.statement: A write outside the allowlist or outside the owner's subtree must not pass ingestion.

sub_cases.evidence: A '..' segment that survives lstrip('./') (because non-dot/slash characters precede it) is caught by `'..' in normalised.split('/')` (control_plane.py:141-146).

`path_in_allowlist`/`check_ownership` normalise with `path.strip().lstrip('./')` (control_plane.py:142, 182). Python's `str.lstrip` treats its argument as a *character set*, not a prefix. A content_uri whose leading run consists only of '.' and '/' characters (e.g. '../workstreams/po03/control/units/attacker/x') has that entire run stripped, leaving a normalised string that starts with an allowed/owned prefix and contains no residual '..' component -- so both the allowlist and ownership checks pass. But the RAW string is what is actually joined to artifact_root (`artifact_root / relative`, control_plane.py:558) and the OS resolves the '..' literally, walking out of the repo root before descending back into a path that only *looks* like it is inside the owner's subtree. The test plants a decoy file as a sibling of the scratch repo root (genuinely outside it) and shows ingest_result accepts and verifies it.
sub_cases.companion_case: TestInv6AllowlistAndOwnershipEscape.test_c_string_level_divergence_absolute_path shows the same class of bug for an absolute content_uri: pathlib's `/` operator discards the left operand entirely when the right operand is absolute, so artifact_root is silently ignored, while the string checks (which also lstrip the leading '/') judge it in-allowlist and owned.
sub_cases.root_cause: The path-scope guard's normalisation (character-class lstrip) is not equivalent to the path semantics actually used for the filesystem join. Any validator that must reason about the same string a filesystem call will use has to apply the *same* normalisation (e.g. os.path.normpath / Path.resolve with a containment check) to both, not a weaker character-strip to one and raw interpretation to the other.
sub_cases.severity_note: This is the single highest-value finding in this audit: it directly breaks the custody guarantee that 'a subordinate cannot write outside its owned subtree or the commission allowlist' (control_plane.py module docstring, line 23-24) and 'The controller re-checks ownership at ingestion, so a subordinate that writes outside its subtree cannot enter shared custody even if its own worktree accepted the write' (path-ownership.json 'rule' field). Both claims are false for a crafted content_uri.

invariants.statement: A producer must not accept its own work.
invariants.result: PARTIALLY BROKEN (boundary, not a full break)

sub_cases.evidence: The guard is a byte-equality string comparison against the dispatch record's `owner` field. There is no mechanism binding `--reviewer` to any authenticated caller identity (no credential, token, or process-level check), so the same actor that produced the work can self-review by invoking `review` with any string other than the exact owner id, and the CLI accepts it. Stopped precisely at: byte-equal owner strings only.
sub_cases.root_cause: Identity throughout control_plane.py (owner, worker_id, reviewer, actor) is an unauthenticated, caller-supplied string. This affects INV-7 directly and is the same mechanism that lets `cmd_complete` hardcode `actor='coordinator'` regardless of which process actually invokes it (control_plane.py:629) -- there is no code-level barrier preventing any process capable of executing the script from invoking `complete`, `ingest`, or `review`; the 'only the coordinator sets COMPLETED' rule is enforced by convention/process topology, not by the tool.

invariants.statement: A tampered ledger row must not pass chain verification.

sub_cases.evidence: Editing a row's payload without recomputing row_sha256/prev_sha256 breaks verify_chain's per-row hash check (control_plane.py:206-209).

verify_chain (control_plane.py:197-211) only checks internal self-consistency: each row's own row_sha256 matches its canonical body, and prev_sha256 chains to the immediately preceding row. There is no externally anchored checkpoint (e.g. a previously git-committed head hash recorded outside the mutable file itself). An actor with write access to ledger.jsonl can therefore edit one row's event/payload (e.g. flip REJECTED to ACCEPTED) and cascade-recompute row_sha256/prev_sha256 for every subsequent row, producing a file that is fully self-consistent end-to-end. `cmd_verify` reports it valid.
sub_cases.root_cause: Hash-chaining alone (without an external anchor such as a signed/pinned prior head, or reliance on git's own immutable history as the actual source of truth rather than the working-tree file) only proves internal consistency, not non-tampering by a party with filesystem write access to the whole file.
sub_cases.mitigating_factor: Because ledger.jsonl is itself git-tracked, a wholesale rewrite would appear as a large diff in git history and could be caught by a reviewer diffing commits -- but that protection lives in the surrounding git workflow and human/automated review discipline, not in control_plane.py's own verify_chain function, which is exactly what this unit was asked to test.

invariants.statement: A PROVIDER_COMPLETED_UNCOMMITTED unit must never be reported as COMPLETED.

sub_cases.evidence: validate_contracts.validate_result forces obzio_state == PROVIDER_COMPLETED_UNCOMMITTED whenever provider_state == COMPLETED and result_commit_id is empty (validate_contracts.py:192-196).

The schema guard above is satisfied by ANY non-empty string in result_commit_id -- it never checks that the string refers to a real, resolvable git commit. ingest_result re-hashes whatever file currently exists on disk at the claimed path (control_plane.py:556-567) but performs no `git cat-file -e <sha>` or equivalent existence check against the claimed result_commit_id. The scratch repo in this test has no `.git` directory at all (asserted explicitly), so no result_commit_id in it could possibly be real; a syntactically well-formed but entirely fabricated 40-hex-character string is accepted, and the unit reaches COMPLETED.
sub_cases.root_cause: 'Committed to git' is asserted by the producer's self-report and never independently verified by the control plane against actual git object storage. The durability guarantee the whole protocol exists to provide (COMMISSION.md: 'the result is committed to a deterministic po03/* remote branch or ingested by the controller') is not mechanically checked here at all -- only the working-tree file's current bytes are checked, which is a strictly weaker property than durable git commitment and does not survive the working tree being discarded.

aggregate_defects: D1 (INV-6, highest severity): character-class lstrip normalisation in path_in_allowlist/check_ownership diverges from the raw-string filesystem join used for real I/O, letting a crafted content_uri (relative '../' runs, or an absolute path) pass allowlist+ownership checks while the actual verified/read file lives outside the repo root and the owner's subtree.

D2 (INV-9): result_commit_id is never checked against real git history; a fabricated commit id over a purely working-tree (never git-committed) artifact reaches COMPLETED, which is precisely the PROVIDER_COMPLETED_UNCOMMITTED failure mode the whole protocol exists to prevent.

D3 (INV-2b): fence-token checking is monotonicity-only; it does not verify the submitted fence_token was ever actually issued by a `lease` call, so an unleased actor can commit by guessing/reading the current high-water mark from the (readable) ledger.

D4 (INV-3b): result deduplication keys on a hash of the entire document rather than unit identity, and the state projection has no terminal-state monotonicity guard, so a semantically different resubmission after COMPLETED is accepted and can be completed a second time with different underlying artifacts.

D5 (INV-8b): the ledger's hash chain has no external anchor, so a cascade-rehashed rewrite of ledger.jsonl is internally self-consistent and passes verify_chain; tamper-evidence for this class of attack currently depends entirely on the surrounding git workflow, not on the tool.

D6 (INV-7b, boundary not break): no caller-identity authentication exists anywhere in the CLI; 'coordinator', 'reviewer', and 'owner' are all unauthenticated strings supplied at the command line, so the commission's 'only the coordinator sets COMPLETED' and 'producer cannot accept own work' rules are enforced by process/topology convention, not by control_plane.py itself.
what_was_not_attacked: Concurrency / true multi-process race conditions on the ledger append (append_event re-reads and re-verifies the chain each call, but this audit did not attempt concurrent writers racing on the same file descriptor from separate OS processes; a2-u07's dispatch record specifically claims this territory and is evaluated under a10-u01 against a2's own concurrency fixture, not duplicated here).
Denial-of-service / resource-exhaustion attacks (e.g. extremely large ledgers, pathological JSON) -- out of scope for the 9 named invariants.

The `create`, `event`, `scan`, and `check-paths` subcommands were exercised incidentally (via create_unit/lease helpers and INV-6's allowlist checks) but were not independently adversarially targeted beyond what the 9 named invariants required.
